_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gold-miner signals with Newmont's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Newmont is one of the world’s largest gold producers and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and the Fortune 500, and has been included in the Dow Jones Sustainability World Index for seven consecutive years.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold and copper, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2013 10-K's own words, which the 8-K of 2014-06-13 recasting its Items 6-8 leaves standing; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty

(the FY2013 10-K's own words, which the 8-K of 2014-06-13 recasting its Items 6-8 leaves standing; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.06x; -47% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.88; conservative 2yr +154%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -36.2%/yr (worst year FY04-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -13.7%/yr (Q2 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY07 ex-FY11 ex-FY13 median

BULL.desc: EPS +18.9%/yr (FY04-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +59.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY04-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEM (retrospective, 2014-09-26) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.06x (54.4% downside to Bear $10.86 / +860.8% upside to Bull $228.76) | Adj composite 3.05 vs market 1.17: gap +1.88 [UNDERVALUED] | -47% above the EPP floor $45.12 (12x FY14E $3.76) | Conservative 2-yr case: +153.5% total (+76.8%/yr) | At 6.3x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $31.49 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue -12.5% YoY in Q2 2014, forward revenues -12.5% (Q2 2014 revenue growth (no revenue guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
